title: Future Plans, Predictions and Healthy Habits
subtitle: A B1 practice pack on will, be going to, the 21-Day Challenge and mental-health vocabulary.
lessonNotes: Use will for a quick decision, offer, promise or a prediction without present evidence: I will help you and I think it will rain.
Use be going to for an intention or a prediction with evidence: I am going to start a challenge; Look at the glass — it is going to fall.
For now, practise only will and be going to. Present simple and present continuous for future meaning will come later.
Healthy-habit vocabulary from the lesson includes break a habit, take up a hobby, cope with stress, mental health, stamina and endurance.
A 21-Day Challenge is a useful context for plans: What are you going to change? What will help you continue?

grammar.title: Will: decisions, offers and predictions
grammar.rule: Use will for a decision made now, an offer or promise, and a prediction based on opinion rather than visible evidence.
examples: I will help you with the challenge.
I think the habit will be difficult at first.

grammar.title: Be going to: intention and evidence
grammar.rule: Use be going to for a plan you already have or a prediction supported by what you can see now.
examples: Mira is going to take up swimming.
The cat is going to knock over the glass.
We are going to try the 21-Day Challenge.

grammar.title: Feelings, needs and preferences
grammar.rule: Love, like, dislike, hate, prefer, want, need, wish and mind usually describe an internal state, so the simple form is normal.

grammar.title: Senses and appearance
grammar.rule: See, hear, smell, taste, feel, seem, appear, look and sound are often stative when they describe passive perception or appearance.

grammar.title: Possession, connection and composition
grammar.rule: Have, own, possess, belong, contain, include, consist, involve and depend usually describe possession or relationships rather than actions.

grammar.title: Measurement, value and identity
grammar.rule: Cost, weigh, measure, fit, equal, matter, deserve, resemble, be and exist are commonly stative when they report a fact or condition.

grammar.title: When -ing becomes possible
grammar.rule: A normally stative verb can use a continuous form when it gains an active, temporary or deliberately changing meaning.
examples: Sam is being unusually patient today.

grammar.title: Play, go and do with sport
grammar.rule: Choose the collocation, not the sport alone. Play usually goes with games and ball/racket sports; go goes with -ing activities; do goes with martial arts, gymnastics, yoga and boxing. Learn common exceptions as fixed phrases.

remember: Ask what the verb means in this sentence. If it names a state, fact, possession, opinion or passive sense, choose the simple form. If it names an activity happening around now, the continuous form may be correct.
watchOut: Marketing and very informal speech sometimes use forms such as I am loving it. Learn the standard pattern first: I love it. Also remember that have can be continuous for activities such as having lunch, but not for possession: I have a fast car.

dailyUsage.actionExample: I am thinking about joining a boxing class.
dailyUsage.tip: Do not say I am thinking it is exciting when you simply mean this is my opinion.

dailyUsage.stateExample: Nadia has a new yoga mat.
dailyUsage.actionMeaning: take part in an activity or experience
dailyUsage.actionExample: Nadia is having a swimming lesson.
dailyUsage.tip: Meals, showers, lessons and a good time can be activities; possession cannot.

dailyUsage.actionExample: I am seeing the physiotherapist tomorrow.
dailyUsage.tip: The continuous form changes see from passive perception to an arranged or repeated meeting.

dailyUsage.actionExample: The coach is tasting the team meal.
dailyUsage.tip: The drink is not doing an action; the coach is.

dailyUsage.actionExample: Ravi is smelling the sports shirt to check it.
dailyUsage.tip: Smell is dynamic when someone actively uses their nose.

dailyUsage.stateMeaning: have an opinion, emotion or physical condition
dailyUsage.stateExample: I feel tired after a long run.
dailyUsage.actionExample: Mira is feeling the rope before climbing.
dailyUsage.tip: I am feeling tired is possible when emphasising a temporary experience, but I feel tired is the safe everyday choice.

dailyUsage.actionExample: Leo is looking at the race results.
dailyUsage.tip: Look meaning appear is followed by an adjective; look at names an action.

dailyUsage.stateMeaning: describe identity or a usual quality
dailyUsage.actionMeaning: behave temporarily in a particular way
dailyUsage.actionExample: Ana is being very patient with the new players today.
dailyUsage.tip: Being plus an adjective usually highlights temporary behaviour, not a permanent trait.

dailyUsage.actionExample: The trainer is weighing the kettlebell.
dailyUsage.tip: The equipment has a weight; a person or machine performs the measuring action.

dailyQuestions.q: Choose the natural opinion about a sport.
opt: I am thinking volleyball is exciting.
dailyQuestions.why: Think meaning have an opinion is stative.

dailyQuestions.q: The activity is happening now. Choose the natural sentence.
opt: Mila is having a swimming lesson.
Mila has a swimming lesson right now.
dailyQuestions.a: Mila is having a swimming lesson.
dailyQuestions.why: Have can be continuous for an activity or experience.

opt: Jon is having a fast bicycle.

dailyQuestions.q: A coach is checking the sauce for the team meal now.
opt: The coach is tasting the sauce.
The coach tastes the sauce every second now.
dailyQuestions.a: The coach is tasting the sauce.
dailyQuestions.why: Taste is an active process here.

opt: The new trainers are looking comfortable.
The new trainers look at comfortable.

dailyQuestions.q: Choose the deliberate action happening now.

dailyQuestions.a: Tara is smelling the sports shirt.

dailyQuestions.q: Choose the normal sentence about weight.

dailyQuestions.why: Weigh meaning have a weight is stative.

opt: Omar is being unusually patient with the new players today.
Omar being unusually patient with the new players today.
Omar is unusually patient with the new players every day today.
dailyQuestions.a: Omar is being unusually patient with the new players today.
dailyQuestions.why: Be can be continuous for deliberate or temporary behaviour.

practice.q: You decide at this moment to begin a new habit. Choose the natural sentence.
opt: I will start a 21-Day Challenge today.
I am going to start a 21-Day Challenge today because I see the result.
I will to start a 21-Day Challenge today.
practice.a: I will start a 21-Day Challenge today.
practice.why: Use will for a decision made at the moment of speaking.

practice.q: Choose the sentence about an intention.
opt: I am going to take up yoga this month.
I will going to take up yoga this month.
I am going take up yoga this month.
practice.a: I am going to take up yoga this month.
practice.why: Use be going to for a plan or intention.

practice.q: There is clear evidence: the glass is at the edge of the table. Choose the natural prediction.
practice.why: Use be going to when you can see evidence now.

opt: Walking helps me cope with stress.
Walking helps me cope at stress.
practice.a: Walking helps me cope with stress.
practice.why: The fixed phrase is cope with stress.

opt: This exercise strengthens your back muscles.
This exercise is strengthening your back muscles every day.
This exercise strengthen your back muscles.
practice.a: This exercise strengthens your back muscles.
practice.why: Use the present simple for a general effect.

opt: Maya is really liking going climbing.
practice.why: Like is normally stative; really comes before like.

opt: Nico does not mind doing the dishes after training.
Nico is not minding doing the dishes after training.
Nico does not mind do the dishes after training.
practice.a: Nico does not mind doing the dishes after training.
practice.why: Mind is stative, and mind is followed by an -ing activity.

opt: I cannot stand running in heavy rain.
I am not standing running in heavy rain.
I cannot standing running in heavy rain.
practice.a: I cannot stand running in heavy rain.
practice.why: Cannot stand expresses a strong dislike.

opt: Sara plays chess with her brother.
Sara goes chess with her brother.
Sara does chess with her brother.
practice.a: Sara plays chess with her brother.

opt: Ben burns calories when he goes swimming.
Ben burns calories at he goes swimming.
Ben burns at calories when he goes swimming.
practice.a: Ben burns calories when he goes swimming.
practice.why: Burn calories is a common health collocation.

opt: I think you look ready for the race.
I am thinking you are looking ready for the race.
I think you are look ready for the race.
practice.a: I think you look ready for the race.
practice.why: Think expresses an opinion and look describes appearance.

opt: I should stretch before I run.
I should to stretch before I run.
I should stretching before I run.
practice.a: I should stretch before I run.
practice.why: Use the base verb after should, without to.

reading.title: Two Ways to Train
reading.text:
Sophie plays volleyball twice a week at a community sports centre. She enjoys the team atmosphere, but she knows that a good warm-up matters before every match. On Wednesday, the team is practising serves because a local tournament starts soon. Sophie usually feels nervous before a competition, yet today she is being very patient with a new player who does not understand the rotation. After practice, Sophie does a few stretching exercises, drinks water and goes home. She believes that regular training strengthens her muscles and helps her cope with stress.

On Sunday, Ilya goes cycling with his cousin along the river. They prefer this route because it is quiet and the hills are not too steep. Ilya owns an old bicycle, but its brakes work well and the helmet fits him perfectly. At the moment, he is checking the tyres because one of them feels soft. His cousin suggests a longer route, but Ilya does not mind changing the plan. They stop after an hour, eat a sandwich and talk about trying judo next month. Ilya thinks judo sounds challenging, while his cousin is thinking about joining a yoga class.

questions.q: How often does Sophie play volleyball?
questions.why: The first sentence gives her routine.

questions.q: Why is Sophie's team practising serves?
questions.why: The first paragraph explains the reason.

questions.q: What does Sophie do after practice?
questions.why: The text lists her actions after practice.

questions.q: Why does Ilya prefer the river route?
opt: It is quiet and the hills are not too steep.
It is the shortest route to the library.
questions.a: It is quiet and the hills are not too steep.
questions.why: The second paragraph gives both reasons.
He is checking them because one feels soft.

questions.q: What does ‘Ilya does not mind changing the plan’ mean?
opt: He is happy to accept a different route.
questions.a: He is happy to accept a different route.
questions.why: Do not mind means that a change is acceptable.

questions.q: Which activity is Ilya's cousin considering?
questions.why: Is thinking about shows active consideration.

listening.title: Choosing a New Sport
listening.instructions: Listen once for the sports choices. Listen again for play, go, do and the verb meanings. Then unlock the transcript and check your answers.
listening.script:
Maya: Are you doing anything active this weekend, Leo?
Leo: I am playing basketball with some colleagues on Saturday. I do not usually play very well, but I really enjoy it.
Maya: Nice. I prefer going cycling because it helps me cope with stress.
Leo: That sounds good. Are you going cycling tomorrow?
Maya: No, I am seeing my sister tomorrow. We are choosing a yoga class together.
Leo: Do you think yoga is difficult?
Maya: I think the first lesson looks easy, but I am thinking about doing it twice a week.
Leo: My brother does yoga. He says it strengthens his back and improves his balance.
Maya: Great. You can play basketball, and I can go cycling. Then we can compare our new routines next week.

questions.q: What is Leo doing on Saturday?
questions.why: Leo says that he is playing basketball with colleagues.

opt: It helps her cope with stress.
questions.a: It helps her cope with stress.

questions.q: What does Maya mean by I am seeing my sister tomorrow?
opt: She has an arranged meeting with her sister.
She can see her sister from far away.
She is studying the word sister.
questions.a: She has an arranged meeting with her sister.
questions.why: See can be continuous when it means meet.
Am thinking about shows active consideration.

questions.q: What benefit does Leo's brother mention?
opt: Yoga strengthens his back and improves balance.
questions.a: Yoga strengthens his back and improves balance.

writing.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional person's weekly sport or fitness routine. Explain which activities they play, go or do, and why. Use at least three health-and-fitness expressions, one temporary behaviour with is being, one normally stative verb, and one active -ing meaning such as is thinking about or is having. Finish with a natural question about sport.
checklist: Use play, go and do correctly
Include three health or fitness expressions
Use is being for temporary behaviour
